activation.reason: This public blueprint has no tenant binding, private evidence store, deployment identities, production approvers, or activated CI/apply path.
blockingDecisions: Bind accountable roles to approved private identities.
Pin every selected runtime, provider, module, script, and test-pack digest.
Select the private enterprise CI runner, state backend, policy engine, signing service, authorization-consumption ledger and independent reader, alert channel, and leadership renderer.
Approve Graph permissions, Intune scope tags, ring limits, privacy aggregation floors, retention, and break-glass controls.

Inventory and assign non-overlapping ownership for Group Policy, Configuration Manager/co-management, Defender security-settings management, Windows servicing, OEM management, Ansible, emergency automation, and Conditional Access dependencies.
Qualify every Microsoft Graph endpoint used for Intune against the pinned provider and API version.
Run and retain all seven real-hardware integration checks.

classificationDefinitions.INTUNE_ENFORCEMENT: The sole authority that enforces Intune-owned endpoint domains.
classificationDefinitions.TRANSPORT_ONLY: Carries an approved request or observation but owns no endpoint policy and cannot broaden scope.
classificationDefinitions.ORCHESTRATION_ONLY: Composes, plans, or invokes an approved transition but is not an endpoint enforcement authority.
classificationDefinitions.INTUNE_DELEGATED_PATH: Implements a named Intune-owned domain only through the Intune enforcement boundary and its approved assignments.
classificationDefinitions.BENCH_OR_NON_INTUNE_ONLY: May change only bench systems or an explicitly approved endpoint domain that Intune does not own.
classificationDefinitions.BOUNDED_EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY: Owns writes only in a named non-endpoint system of record, custody, review, signing, or notification boundary.
classificationDefinitions.NONE: Has no authority to change enterprise endpoint configuration; artifact or evidence output does not create endpoint authority.

rules: Exactly one checked-in binding is classified INTUNE_ENFORCEMENT.
Every checked-in toolId has exactly one classification and no unknown toolId may be classified.
Transport and orchestration tools cannot originate, broaden, or self-approve endpoint scope.
An Intune-delegated path remains subordinate to the approved Intune object, assignment, ring, and readback controls.
Bench or non-Intune changes require an explicit ownership boundary and cannot overlap an Intune-owned endpoint domain.
A new or reclassified endpoint writer produces HOLD until this policy, its tests, and the private activation record are approved.
Every managed Intune object type has exactly one selected transport in the private ownership record.
The Microsoft Graph Terraform provider is the default only after lifecycle, import, API-version, throttling, and readback qualification for that object type.
The direct Graph adapter is an expiring exception path for explicitly listed provider gaps and may not overlap the provider path for the same object type and scope.
Neither transport owns policy intent, expands target scope, self-approves, or substitutes Terraform state for independent Graph readback.
An empty objectTypeOwnership inventory is an activation blocker, not permission to choose a path at runtime.

bindings.identityBoundary: Read-only public source by default; no cloud, Graph, evidence-store, or bench identity.
bindings.failureMode: Unavailable review remains pending; it never becomes approval.
bindings.replacementRule: A replacement must preserve sandboxing, source citation, question history, and non-approval boundary.

roles: inventory effective policy and residual production ownership
identify overlap with Intune settings
bindings.writeScope: no Intune-owned production field; any retained non-Intune domain requires explicit private ownership and scope
prohibitedUses: use processing order as conflict governance
treat policy existence as device effectiveness
bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation inventories policy IDs, backups, precedence, scope, owners, change history, and effective-state collection method.
bindings.identityBoundary: Domain policy administration remains separate from Intune write and readback identities.
bindings.failureMode: Unknown or overlapping policy ownership keeps the affected domain on HOLD.
bindings.replacementRule: Migration must preserve policy intent, effective-state evidence, rollback, and non-overlap proof.

roles: inventory co-management workload authority
identify applications, scripts, updates, and settings still managed outside Intune
bindings.writeScope: no Intune-owned production field; retained workloads require explicit private non-overlapping ownership
prohibitedUses: co-manage the same field without an owner
inherit pilot scope from a collection
treat deployment submission as endpoint success
bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation pins client, site, workload sliders, collection rules, packages, deployments, and readback queries.
bindings.identityBoundary: Site administration and client authority remain separate from Intune automation and evidence release.
bindings.failureMode: Unknown co-management authority or overlapping workload ownership keeps promotion on HOLD.
bindings.replacementRule: Migration must preserve package identity, membership, deployment evidence, rollback, and one-writer proof.

bindings.product: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management
roles: inventory security policies delivered through the Defender channel
prove Intune and Defender ownership do not overlap
bindings.writeScope: only explicitly delegated security-policy objects within the approved Intune ownership and assignment boundary

readback.scopeRule: both service-side assignment and device-side state must match

prohibitedUses: create a second owner for an Intune security field
bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation pins enrollment mode, policy IDs, assignment rules, API/report versions, and device-side verification.
bindings.identityBoundary: Defender policy administration and readback are separately scoped and audited.
bindings.failureMode: Unknown delegation, overlap, stale state, or scope mismatch blocks the affected security policy.
bindings.replacementRule: A replacement must preserve policy ownership, service/device readback, conflict detection, and rollback.

bindings.product: Approved OEM driver, firmware, and endpoint-management service
roles: inventory OEM agents, schedules, repositories, and write authority
bind firmware and driver changes to requalification
bindings.writeScope: only privately approved firmware or driver domains that do not overlap the selected Windows servicing owner
bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation pins product, catalog, policy, repository, agent, signer, schedule, scope, and rollback behavior.
bindings.identityBoundary: OEM administration is tenant-private, least-privilege, and separate from evidence approval.
bindings.failureMode: Unowned, unexpected, or unobserved firmware/driver mutation produces HOLD and requalification review.
bindings.replacementRule: A replacement must preserve catalog provenance, bounded scope, device readback, rollback, and trigger mapping.

roles: perform a specifically authorized emergency endpoint action
record and reconcile every changed field
bindings.writeScope: one approved incident, action digest, field set, target snapshot, and validity window; no standing Intune overlap

readback.scopeRule: independent service and device readback as applicable

bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation pins runner, action digest, signer, incident, approvals, expiry, target snapshot, audit, and reconciliation SLA.
bindings.identityBoundary: JIT break-glass identity with independent approval, monitoring, revocation, and post-use review.
bindings.failureMode: Missing approval, scope, expiry, readback, or reconciliation blocks or rolls back the action.
bindings.replacementRule: A replacement must preserve JIT authorization, exact action and scope binding, independent readback, and reconciliation.

roles: consume Intune compliance signals
enforce separately governed access policy
bindings.writeScope: Entra access policy only; never an endpoint configuration or qualification verdict authority
prohibitedUses: treat access success as endpoint compliance proof
bindings.versionPolicy: Private activation pins policy IDs, conditions, exclusions, report-only results, break-glass exclusions, and Graph API versions.
bindings.identityBoundary: Access-policy administration is separate from endpoint writer, compliance evaluator, and directory readback identities.
bindings.failureMode: Unknown or mismatched access dependency blocks claims about effective compliance or rollout access.
bindings.replacementRule: A replacement must preserve access-policy separation, report-only validation, exclusions, audit, and independent readback.

bindings.product: Organization EDR, DLP, ZTNA/VPN, VDI, management, authentication, application, and peripheral matrix
roles: define the exact corporate compatibility and security matrix
bindings.writeScope: deployment only through the tool that owns each product; names remain private
prohibitedUses: hard-code vendor names in portable method
bindings.versionPolicy: Private matrix pins every product, agent, driver, signer, version, assignment, and support status.
bindings.identityBoundary: Product names and configuration remain in private activation/evidence repositories.
bindings.failureMode: Unknown, unsupported, failed, or stale critical dependency blocks Phase 2 unless an authorized exception exists.
bindings.replacementRule: Any stack change maps to staleness dependencies and triggers the applicable compatibility/security rerun.
